clinician.final_diagnosis: Mycoplasma pneumoniae infection presenting with CNS manifestations in the form of stroke and meningoencephalitis, with asymptomatic arterial aneurysms
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 39-year-old Filipino man with no prior comorbidities presented with acute-onset moderate-grade intermittent fever, bifrontal dull aching headache, neck pain, lethargy, and inability to concentrate. On admission, he was febrile (100.6°F) with normal chest and cardiovascular examination. Neurological examination revealed lethargy with coherent speech, normal cranial nerves and focal neurological exam, but positive neck stiffness and Kernig sign indicating meningeal irritation. Laboratory workup showed elevated WBC (10,700/μL with 86% neutrophils), elevated ESR (35 mm/hour), and CSF analysis demonstrating lymphocytic pleocytosis (58 WBCs, 92% lymphocytes) with mildly elevated protein (52 mg/dL) and normal glucose (80 mg/dL). CSF gram stain and culture were negative; HSV and VZV PCR were negative. MRI brain revealed an acute infarct in the left centrum semi-ovale on FLAIR and DWI sequences. Conventional angiography documented asymptomatic aneurysms in the left subclavian artery and aortic arch. Mycoplasma pneumoniae serology confirmed the diagnosis with positive IgM (1:100) and IgG (1:120) antibodies. One week after hospitalization, the patient developed acute right-sided weakness with mild upper motor neuron facial weakness and dysarthria, indicating progression of CNS involvement. Treatment included ceftriaxone and acyclovir initially (discontinued after negative HSV/VZV PCR), aspirin for stroke management, and azithromycin for 5 days after Mycoplasma diagnosis. The patient became afebrile, headache subsided, and sensorium improved after azithromycin initiation. Neurological deficits completely resolved with physiotherapy. final.trajectory_summary: A 39-year-old Filipino man with no prior comorbidities presented with acute-onset moderate-grade intermittent fever, bifrontal dull aching headache, neck pain, lethargy, and inability to concentrate. On admission, he was febrile (100.6°F) with normal chest and cardiovascular examination. Neurological examination revealed lethargy with coherent speech, normal cranial nerves and focal neurological exam, but positive neck stiffness and Kernig sign indicating meningeal irritation. Laboratory workup showed elevated WBC (10,700/μL with 86% neutrophils), elevated ESR (35 mm/hour), and CSF analysis demonstrating lymphocytic pleocytosis (58 WBCs, 92% lymphocytes) with mildly elevated protein (52 mg/dL) and normal glucose (80 mg/dL). CSF gram stain and culture were negative; HSV and VZV PCR were negative. MRI brain revealed an acute infarct in the left centrum semi-ovale on FLAIR and DWI sequences. Conventional angiography documented asymptomatic aneurysms in the left subclavian artery and aortic arch. Mycoplasma pneumoniae serology confirmed the diagnosis with positive IgM (1:100) and IgG (1:120) antibodies. One week after hospitalization, the patient developed acute right-sided weakness with mild upper motor neuron facial weakness and dysarthria, indicating progression of CNS involvement. Treatment included ceftriaxone and acyclovir initially (discontinued after negative HSV/VZV PCR), aspirin for stroke management, and azithromycin for 5 days after Mycoplasma diagnosis. The patient became afebrile, headache subsided, and sensorium improved after azithromycin initiation. Neurological deficits completely resolved with physiotherapy. The patient was asymptomatic at 1-month and 3-month follow-up.
